<subject>Re: Results of the Bankruptcy Hearing for Northern Financial's Issues With Corporate Lending</subject>
<body>
You should have the email below in your inbox talking about the clients on the Halcyon General Ledger. Reply to the email below once you find out if you are able to use the client's funds without maintaining a minimum balance.
</body>
<quoted>
-----Original Message-----
From: 	Owen, Julia  
Sent:	Tuesday, April 29, 2025 4:09 PM
To:	Hamilton, Derek; Hutchinson, Ross; Johnston, Laura; Marian Hussain, Debra
Cc:	Sophie Jr., Ed; Mann, Gregory; m796@maroragroup.com'; s692@soldynlabs.com'; Barker, Mathew; Amy, Joshua; Garza, Kathleen; m789@trinorco.com'; j244@trinorco.com'; Holmes, Sean A.
Subject:	Results of the Bankruptcy Hearing for Northern Financial's Issues With Corporate Lending

Here is a quick update on how Northern Financial, a client of Consolidated Credit, bankruptcy hearing went last week for the Corporate Lending issues:

Northern Financial agreed to withdraw the portion of their motion that was associated with Corporate Lending. The bank admitted that Corporate Lending has been using their credit lines and have been repaying their loans since the bankruptcy petition date.
The £2.1 million claim that Northern Financial had been including in the Halcyon Mutual Bank "set off amount" (i.e. the remaining demand charges for Corporate Lending's agreements until the end of the contract terms) was pulled out Northern Financial's Motion.
The minimum Treasury/corporate account agreement monthly balance should no longer be required by the bank (Note: Originally Northern Financial appeared to be using Corporate Lending's minimum balance to set off Credit Risk & Corporate Lending obligations). 

I would recommend that you challenge Northern Financial's operations folks, if they continue to say that Corporate Lending must be keeping a minimum balance in your corporate account. If you have any problems, please let me know and I will get our outside counsel involved again.

Thanks,
Julia Owen
</quoted>
